title: Reconstructing hidden GPCR conformations and ligand binding modes through integrative DEER modeling.
one_liner_zh: 该文整合DEER实验数据、深度学习结构预测和分子动力学模拟，重建GPCR隐藏构象及配体结合模式，核心聚焦蛋白质构象采样与结构计算建模，方法创新且可迁移至其他蛋白体系。
abstract: Binding of biased ligands to a G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) stabilizes specific receptor conformations, leading to distinct physiological responses. Recently, intra-transducer bias has emerged as an additional mechanism that fine-tunes receptor function by stabilizing specific architectures of the receptor-transducer complex. This mechanism was demonstrated for the angiotensin receptor (AT1R) and its beta-arrestin-biased ligand TRV026, which selectively promotes beta-arrestin-1 engagement via the receptor C terminus while preventing interaction with the receptor core. Here, we present a computational protocol integrating double electron-electron resonance (DEER) data with deep learning-based structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations to reconstruct all-atom models of TRV026-bound AT1R. Using a new clustering method, we identify key ligand-receptor interactions underlying high-affinity binding, localized receptor flexibility, and ligand bias. Our results provide a framework for validating neural-network predictions and physics-based simulations to capture rare signaling states of membrane proteins and identify target conformations for designing more functionally selective, efficacious therapeutics.
abstract_zh: 偏向性配体与G蛋白偶联受体（GPCR）的结合稳定了特定的受体构象，从而引发不同的生理反应。近期，转导子内偏向性（intra-transducer bias）作为一种额外机制出现，通过稳定受体-转导子复合物的特定结构来微调受体功能。该机制已在血管紧张素受体（AT1R）及其β-arrestin偏向性配体TRV026上得到证实，后者通过受体C末端选择性促进β-arrestin-1结合，同时阻止与受体核心的相互作用。在此，我们提出一种计算协议，整合双电子-电子共振（DEER）数据、基于深度学习的结构预测和分子动力学模拟，以重建TRV026结合的AT1R的全原子模型。利用一种新的聚类方法，我们识别了高亲和力结合、局部受体灵活性和配体偏向性背后的关键配体-受体相互作用。我们的结果为验证神经网络预测和基于物理的模拟提供了框架，以捕获膜蛋白的稀有信号状态，并识别用于设计更具功能选择性和高效治疗药物的靶向构象。
